system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate

- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team (Buyer)
**Bottom line:** The Seller's package departs from our playbook on nearly every point. Taken together, the changes would greatly reduce the Seller's real exposure:
- They cut the cap, multiply the thresholds and shorten the claims period.
- They put title under the general regime and remove any fraud carve-out.
- They deem the whole data room disclosed and add a blanket buyer-knowledge bar.
- They leave Bluefen, Riverlark and the bonuses open at Completion.

We should reject the package as drafted and send a full mark-up.

---

## 1. The "Reviewer Efficiency Note" should be rejected

The Seller's note says clauses marked **[STANDARD]** "have been reviewed and cleared by both sides". It asks us to review only **[OPEN]** items and to treat the disclosure and limitation framework as "already accepted".

**We should not proceed on that basis.**

- Nothing in our playbook records agreement to any of these positions. Almost every [STANDARD] item departs from our stated position.
- No clause in the package is actually marked [OPEN]. If we followed the note, we would review nothing.
- The labels are the Seller's own drafting. They do not record agreement. Any clause becomes agreed only when we agree it.

**Action:** Say expressly in our response that we do not accept the [STANDARD] classifications or the statement that the disclosure and limitation framework has been accepted. Separately, confirm internally whether anyone on our side has informally agreed any point. I am assuming no one has.

---

## 2. Departures from the playbook

| # | Topic | Seller position | Our playbook | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | General cap (cl 12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m | Seller has opened at our *fallback* |
| 2 | Thresholds (cl 12.2) | De minimis AUD 25k; basket AUD 250k; excess only | De minimis AUD 5k; basket AUD 50k; first dollar | 5x on both, plus deductible instead of tipping basket |
| 3 | Claims period (cl 12.3/13) | 18 months | 24 months | Seller has opened at our *fallback* |
| 4 | Limitations apply to all claims | "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" | Categories kept separate; no hidden override | Catch-all override |
| 5 | Fundamental / Title | Same caps and time limits as general | 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge | Fundamental regime removed |
| 6 | Fraud (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5) | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of everything | **No fraud carve-out at all** |
| 7 | Disclosure (Sch 7 / DL 1.1–1.2) | Whole data room + accounts + statutory registers + public records | Specific fair disclosure only | Deemed general disclosure |
| 8 | Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3) | Blanket bar: Buyer or advisers' knowledge, or anything "discoverable" | Delete | Blanket exclusion |
| 9 | Bluefen (cl 3/6.3) | Reasonable endeavours; satisfied on delivery of consent | Effective consent + evidence conditions met, before Completion | Weaker CP |
| 10 | Riverlark (cl 2/7) | Release "following Completion" | Payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, releases at Completion | Post-completion release |
| 11 | Bonuses (funds flow) | AUD 420k "a matter for the Seller", not itemised | Line item or Seller-funded, including on-costs | Silent exclusion |
| 12 | Ironquay (cl 11.1) | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment | Broaden; keep SOW3 cure | Too narrow |
| 13 | DD-006 incident (cl 4.6/Sch 6) | "Not expected to be material" | Preserve logs, investigate, require updates | Unsupported characterisation |
| 14 | Sandbar | "Ordinary-course operating costs" | Assess; no automatic treatment | Premature conclusion |
| 15 | Tax / IP | "Settled under the general regime" | OPEN, separate categories | Premature closure |
| 16 | Title | Share register DD-012 | Independent evidence | Internal source only |

---

## 3. Issue-by-issue analysis

### 3.1 General cap: hold at 25% / AUD 6,000,000

The Seller proposes 20% / AUD 4.8m. That is exactly our conditional fallback. It also suggests the Seller may know our range, so it is worth checking internally how this figure came to be proposed.

**We have no authority to concede it.** The fallback needs prior written authority from Amelia Frost that identifies the specific draft. None has been given. Respond at 25%.

If the deal team wants to use the fallback later, get Amelia's written approval for this draft first. Even then, trade it for something, such as the threshold or fundamental-regime points, rather than giving it away.

### 3.2 Thresholds: reject

The proposal raises both thresholds five-fold and changes how the basket works.

- **De minimis AUD 25k:** Claims below this are excluded entirely. They also do not count toward the basket, so the two thresholds compound each other.
- **Basket AUD 250k:** This is about 1% of the price, against our 0.2%.
- **"Only the excess is recoverable":** This turns the basket into a deductible. The Seller would never bear the first AUD 250k of valid loss. Our position is a tipping basket: once AUD 50k is exceeded, the Seller is liable from the first dollar.

**Push back:** De minimis AUD 5k; basket AUD 50k; recovery from the first dollar. The playbook has no fallback on thresholds.

### 3.3 Claims period and the catch-all override

**18 months vs 24 months.** As with the cap, the Seller has opened at our fallback, which needs Amelia Frost's written approval. Hold at 24 months.

**"Any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."** This sentence is the most dangerous drafting point in the package.

- It reverses the default. Every cap, threshold and time limit would cover title, tax, IP, specific indemnities, covenants and payment obligations unless each one is expressly excluded.
- Any gap in drafting would favour the Seller.
- It is a hidden general-regime override, which the playbook rejects.

**Push back:** Delete it. Define the general limitations so that they apply only to "General Warranty Claims". List the excluded categories expressly:
- Fundamental/Title Claims
- Tax Claims
- IP Claims
- claims under specific indemnities
- covenant claims
- payment and price-adjustment obligations
- claims involving fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct

### 3.4 Fundamental and Title warranties: reject entirely

"Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to put title and capacity under a 20% cap and an 18-month period. If title fails, we have bought nothing. That loss equals the whole price and may only come to light years later.

**Push back:** Keep a separate fundamental regime:
- 100% cap
- at least six years
- outside the general basket and de minimis
- not subject to any knowledge or disclosure bar

### 3.5 Fraud carve-out: missing, and must be inserted

Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply the limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions to "all Claims of any nature". The draft has no fraud exception anywhere. As written, the Seller could argue that a fraudulent misstatement is capped at AUD 4.8m, time-barred after 18 months, and excluded by non-reliance.

Under Australian law, a party generally cannot rely on a contractual exclusion to escape liability for its own fraud. Non-reliance clauses also do not straightforwardly defeat claims for misleading or deceptive conduct under the Australian Consumer Law. Even so, we should not leave this to litigation.

**Push back:** Insert an express carve-out. Claims arising from fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct of the Seller, its officers, employees, agents or advisers should be excluded from:
- all caps
- baskets and de minimis
- time limits
- the exclusive-remedy clause
- the non-reliance clause

The carve-out should apply "to the maximum extent permitted by law". **This point is non-negotiable and nobody can waive it.** It should not appear in any trade.

### 3.6 Disclosure: reject general disclosure (DL 1.1–1.2)

The Seller proposes to disclose against the warranties:
- everything in the data room as at 22 September 2026
- the Accounts
- the statutory registers
- all publicly searchable corporate records

This deems us to know every fact anywhere in those sources, however buried or unconnected to a particular warranty. The warranties would be largely empty.

**Push back:**
- Delete 1.1 and 1.2. Allow only specific disclosures that fairly disclose each matter, with enough detail for us to identify its nature and scope, against the warranty concerned.
- Paragraphs 2 to 10 are reasonably candid specific disclosures and can largely stay as such. Make clear that no disclosure qualifies the fundamental warranties, the specific indemnities, or the conditions and covenants. For example, disclosing the Ironquay, bonus or incident matters must not cut down the indemnities that deal with them.
- Paragraph 1.4 (non-admission) is acceptable in principle. It must not be read as weakening the specific disclosures.
- **Timing:** The letter speaks as at 22 September 2026, which is now about six weeks old. Require an updated disclosure letter as at signing. Any disclosure between signing and Completion should not cure a warranty breach. At most it should give a termination or notification right.

### 3.7 Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3): delete

The clause bars claims for anything the Buyer **or its advisers** knew, **or anything discoverable** from the data room or public records. Combined with general disclosure, this bars the same claims twice. It also effectively penalises us for doing due diligence, because any fact our advisers saw could defeat a claim.

**Push back:** Delete it. If knowledge qualifiers appear anywhere, they should apply only to the Seller's warranties ("so far as the Seller is aware"). Awareness should be limited to named Seller knowledge persons and should include what they would know after reasonable enquiry. No knowledge qualifier should ever apply to title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.

### 3.8 Bluefen: strengthen the condition

Bluefen accounts for about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue, roughly 30% of the business. Its contract has a change-control consent clause (11.2) with conditions attached (11.3).

The Seller says the consent is "addressed". Its own Disclosure Letter (para 2) says **no final written consent has been provided and there is no evidence that the 11.3 conditions are satisfied.** The two documents are inconsistent, and the Disclosure Letter is the more reliable statement of the facts.

The proposal is weak in two ways:
- Reasonable endeavours alone is too soft for a customer of this size.
- Treating the condition as met "on delivery" of a written consent means a consent that is conditional, qualified or not yet effective would still satisfy it.

**Push back:** Make it a condition precedent to Completion that:
1. Bluefen's written consent under clause 11.2 is effective and unconditional (or subject only to conditions the Buyer approves); and
2. the Buyer receives evidence, satisfactory to it, that every clause 11.3 condition is satisfied.

The condition should be for the Buyer's benefit and waivable only by the Buyer. Add a firmer Seller obligation to procure the consent, plus a long-stop date with a Buyer termination right.

### 3.9 Riverlark: settle at Completion, not after

The facility has about AUD 3.2m outstanding. It contains a change-control clause (8.1) and a discharge clause (9.2). The Disclosure Letter (para 3) confirms it has not been repaid and no discharge is available.

A release "following Completion" means we would pay the price while the target's assets are still encumbered. The change of control could also trigger default under clause 8.1. On a debt-free/cash-free deal, this facility is plainly Debt.

**Push back:** Require all of the following:
- a current payout letter from Riverlark Bank, valid as at the Completion date
- repayment paid directly to Riverlark out of Completion funds as a funds-flow line item, with the amount treated as Debt
- signed deeds of release and PPSR discharges (or a binding commitment to lodge them immediately) delivered at Completion

A post-completion release is possible only with an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark **and** Amelia Frost's approval. Neither is available, so the Seller's current proposal cannot be accepted.

### 3.10 Employee bonuses: AUD 420,000 plus on-costs

The Seller says the DD-005 bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised. The **Company**, however, is presumably the employer. The bonuses fall due on Completion, so the Company would pay them after we own it, unless the funds flow deals with them. Calling them "a matter for the Seller" without any mechanism quietly leaves the cost with us.

The Disclosure Letter (para 5) also says nothing on payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs. The full cost is therefore unquantified.

**Push back:**
- Make the bonuses and all triggered on-costs (PAYG withholding, superannuation, payroll tax, workers' compensation and the like) a specific line item in the funds flow. Either treat them as Debt or Transaction Expenses and deduct them from the price, or have the Seller fund them at Completion.
- Add a specific indemnity for any shortfall.
- Ask the Seller to quantify the on-costs and confirm the payment mechanism, including whether these are payroll payments by the Company. We should not estimate a figure ourselves.

### 3.11 Ironquay IP: broaden the indemnity, keep the SOW3 cure

Under DD-004 clause 7.3, the SOW3 Project Materials transfer only on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 as open. As the Seller itself says, that is not bank-verified. There is no payment receipt and no confirmatory assignment.

An indemnity limited to "the specific SOW3 payment" covers the fee only. It does not cover the real risk, which is that the Company does not own, or cannot use, IP that may be core to the product. That risk includes:
- third-party or Ironquay claims
- injunctions
- rework or replacement cost
- loss from a failed assignment

**Push back:**
- Broaden the indemnity to cover loss from any failure of the Company to own, or hold sufficient rights to, Ironquay-developed materials (SOW3 and any others), and from any Ironquay claim about those materials.
- Keep the SOW3 cure. Before Completion (or as a covenant), the Seller should procure payment of any SOW3 fees genuinely outstanding, with evidence of cleared payment and a signed confirmatory assignment from Ironquay.
- The AUD 180,000 figure is unverified **both ways**. We should not assume it is owed or that it has been paid. Ask for bank evidence and Ironquay's statement of account.
- The IP indemnity should sit outside the general cap and basket. Its exact terms remain open (see 3.15).

### 3.12 DD-006 export/privacy incident

A download link was sent to an unintended external address. The export may contain about 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps).

The Seller calls this "not expected to be material". Its own Disclosure Letter says it is unknown:
- whether anyone accessed the file
- the exact scope
- whether notification is required

The investigation is still preliminary. The "not material" label has no factual basis. Equally, we should **not** treat this as a confirmed breach, assume harm or a notification duty, or put a number on it.

**Push back:**
- Do not accept a materiality characterisation in the SPA or Schedule 6.
- Add Seller covenants to:
  - preserve all relevant logs and evidence
  - continue a proper investigation, including any assessment required under the Privacy Act 1988 notifiable data breach scheme
  - give the Buyer regular written updates and a right to be consulted before any notification or regulator contact
- Keep the data-protection warranties free of general qualification.
- Consider a specific indemnity tied to the incident, with no pre-set figure, sitting outside the general limitation regime.

Privacy counsel should confirm promptly whether the assessment has been completed. Several weeks have passed since 22 September.

### 3.13 Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000)

The Seller asserts these are "ordinary-course operating costs". The Disclosure Letter (para 8) says it does not state whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. It also says DD-008 and DD-011 should be read together.

These are three related renewals of AUD 110,000 each. We should check:
- whether splitting them affects any approval or conduct-of-business threshold
- when they were committed
- whether they are related-party arrangements
- whether they can be terminated

**Push back:** Do not accept the "ordinary course" label. Equally, do not assume they are Debt or that the price should drop. Request the contracts and assess them. Then decide whether they belong in Debt, working capital, conduct-of-business covenants or a specific warranty.

### 3.14 Title: independent evidence required

The DD-012 share register is the Company's own internal record. As the Seller acknowledges, it is the source the Seller relies on, not independent proof.

**Request:**
- current ASIC company extract and historical extracts
- share certificates
- the constitution
- share issue and transfer history with supporting resolutions
- PPSR searches against the Seller and the Company, including confirmation that the Riverlark security does not extend to the shares
- evidence of the Seller's authority and capacity: board resolution and solvency confirmation

Title must sit within the fundamental regime (see 3.4).

### 3.15 Tax and IP: still open

The statement that tax and IP are "settled under the general regime" is not agreed. These terms remain **OPEN**. They must stay separate categories, outside the catch-all limitation override.

We should not assume they resolve as unlimited liability, and we should not assume they resolve in the Seller's favour either. Note that the Seller's rule that "limitations apply to all Claims" (3.3) would close these points by default. That is another reason to delete it.

### 3.16 Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)

The Seller says only a landlord notification is required, and that the Mossvale assignment restriction is not triggered by a share sale. Both readings are plausible but should be checked against the full documents. Add a covenant that the Seller procures the lease notification at or before Completion.

---

## 4. Summary of recommendations

**Points to reject or hold firm on:**
1. **Reject the "Reviewer Efficiency Note"** and the [STANDARD] labels in writing. Nothing in the package is agreed.
2. **Insert a fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out** from all caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance. Not tradeable.
3. **Delete the "limitations apply to all Claims" override.** Keep title, tax, IP, specific indemnity, covenant and payment claims as separate categories.
4. **Restore the fundamental regime** for title and capacity: 100% cap, at least six years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge.
5. **Cap 25% / AUD 6m; claims period 24 months.** Do not offer the 20% or 18-month fallbacks without Amelia Frost's written authority for this draft.
6. **Thresholds AUD 5k / AUD 50k, first dollar.** Reject AUD 25k / AUD 250k / excess-only.
7. **Delete general disclosure (DL 1.1–1.2) and the cl 8.3 buyer-knowledge bar.** Specific fair disclosure only, with an updated letter at signing.

**Completion mechanics:**
8. **Bluefen:** CP requiring effective consent plus evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, before Completion and waivable only by the Buyer.
9. **Riverlark:** current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, releases at Completion. No post-completion release without an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia's approval.
10. **Bonuses:** AUD 420k plus all on-costs itemised in the funds flow (Debt or Seller-funded), backed by an indemnity.

**Specific risks:**
11. **Ironquay:** broaden the indemnity to cover IP ownership and claims, keep the SOW3 cure, and obtain bank evidence and a confirmatory assignment. Treat the AUD 180k as unverified.
12. **DD-006:** strike "not material"; add covenants on log preservation, investigation and updates. Make no assumption of breach and set no figure.
13. **Sandbar:** request the contracts and assess them. No automatic Debt or price treatment.
14. **Title:** independent evidence (ASIC, certificates, PPSR, authority); DD-012 alone is not enough.
15. **Tax and IP:** keep open and separate. No resolution implied in either direction.

**Internal follow-ups:**
- Confirm nobody has informally agreed any [STANDARD] point.
- Consider why the Seller's opening cap and claims period match our confidential fallbacks exactly.
- Escalate to Amelia Frost only if the team wants authority to use either fallback, with the specific draft identified.
- Brief privacy counsel on the status of the DD-006 assessment.
=== END ADVICE ===
